text.p: Home furnishings products maker Fieldcrest Cannon Inc said on Thursday that it expects its proposed sale of assets of its blanket division to Pillowtex Corp to proceed despite union attempts to block the deal on antitrust grounds.

UNITE, a Washington-based organization that represents 3,500 Fieldcrest Cannon workers and 530 Pillowtex workers, filed a petition with the Federal Trade Commission. Fieldcrest Cannon announced on October 4, that it agreed to sell certain blanket division inventories and equipment to Dallas-based Pillowtex for about $30 million cash.

"We are not aware of anything that's going to change what we've said about the blanket division," said Dick Reece, Fieldcrest Cannon vice president of human resources. "As far as we're concerned the two parties have an ongoing agreement.
UNITE (Union of Needletrades, Industrial and Textile Employees) claimed 750 Fieldcrest Cannon workers would lose their jobs in the sale,

"The sale of Fieldcrest's blanket operations to Pillowtex will increase industry concentration, remove excess capacity and will allow Pillowtex to consolidate its hold on the industry," said Michale Zucker of UNITE.
"This transaction is a classic antirtrust situation," Zucker added.
But Reece said Eden, N.C.-based Fieldcrest Cannon was studying options to keep the 750 workers after the plant closes next month. A specific date was not disclosed.
"The plans are right now to close those operations at the end of November. We're currently having discussions about placing those workers elsewhere in the Eden area," he said.
UNITE's petition said the sale would allow Pillowtex to control nearly 66 percent of the blanket market and create unfair competition in the blanket industry.
The petition also said closing blanket facilities in Eden would lessen manufacturing capacity and enhance Pillowtex' ability to raise prices for blankets unfairly.
Fieldcrest Cannon sells products under Fieldcrest, Cannon, Royal Velvet and other labels including private brands.
Pillowtex will sell blankets, throws, bed pillows and mattress pads with Fieldcrest Cannon's brands and other marks under a long-term trademark license royalty agreement.
Shares of Fieldcrest ended up 1/4 at 13-1/2, while Pillowtex was flat at 14-1/8.
